title: Mutation fixture declaration
description: One entry in the mutation catalogue of docs/sdd/05-evaluation-plan.md, with the lifecycle state defined in its section 1a. Constitution Article III says a gate without a killing fixture does not exist; this file is what makes that checkable, because a gate whose fixture was never written and a gate whose fixture was deleted are otherwise indistinguishable from an empty directory.

id.description: The catalogue identifier. Must appear in the evaluation plan's table.

state.description: Lifecycle state (evaluation plan section 1a). 'reserved': the identifier and intent exist, the gate does not. 'partial': one component owns part of the check and blocks at that layer, and the fixture is not counted toward hard-gate coverage. 'active': the gate exists and the fixture proves it blocks. 'retired': superseded, which needs an ADR.

phase.description: Delivery phase that owns the gate.

gate.description: The rule this fixture must find broken.

mutation.description: What is changed to break it.

expected.description: What the harness must do instead. A fixture whose expectation is 'something fails' kills nothing.

owned_here.description: Required on 'partial': the clause this build does enforce.

still_missing.description: Required on 'partial': the clause it does not, and who lands it. Named so that a partial fixture cannot quietly be read as full coverage.

superseded_by.description: Required on 'retired': the ADR that withdrew this fixture. Retiring a killing fixture is a decision, not a cleanup.
